messages:
amanda: Heads up — we've started seeing cluster-autoscaler hangups when burst-scaling mixed MIG/time-slice nodepools in eu-west-1. Pods stay Pending even though there should be capacity. Anyone seen this pattern?

dinesh: Yup, saw a couple of those yesterday. Usually manifests as a scale-up event triggered but new nodes staying NotReady or kubelet flapping.

sasha: Is this the new 'burstbinpacking' config we rolled out? (separate nodepools with binpacking + burst policy)

amanda: Yes — one pool is mig-4g/time-slice, label gpu.slice=short-burst; another is mig-4g/dedicated, label gpu.slice=full. Autoscaler policy tries to prefer short-burst but then packs jobs and stalls.

infra-bot: autoscaler-bot reports: scaleUp: triggered 3->6 nodes (reason: Pending pods match resources), but 2 nodes failed readiness checks (kubelet: CrashLoopBackOff).

kai: Two quick suspects: 1) Node boot network MTU mismatch in that AZ (eu-west-1c) causing CNI overlay to drop kubelet heartbeats; 2) We might be saturating ephemeral NVMe on the burst machines and kubelet OOMs on the cri runtime.

dinesh: Good call. I noticed we set hostNetwork: false for the probe sidecar in those workloads — combined with small slice durations the probe timing is tight. Also our bootstrap script has a race: docker-vers mismatch + nvidia-driver install sometimes delays nodeReady beyond 5m and autoscaler abandons?

sasha: We should check the nodepool startup script in the burst pools. If nvdriver-install is synchronous it should block kubelet until done. If not, kubelet starts without GPU plugin and pods wait indefinitely.

amanda: Reproduced locally: when the GPU plugin pod crashes, the scheduler marks GPU resources allocatable=0 and CA keeps trying new nodes. Caused a churn loop.

autoscaler-bot: note: cluster-autoscaler 1.27.0 has a known issue with mixed resource types and delayed allocatable updates (see internal runbook: https://rwd.co/runbook/ca-mixed-alloc).

kai: Short-term mitigation: (1) Add a nodepool-level taint to prevent binpacked jobs from landing on burst-slice pools: kubectl patch nodepool burst --patch '{"spec":{"taints":[{"key":"slice","value":"burst","effect":"NoSchedule"}]}}' ; (2) Increase CA scaleUpDelay and reduce maxEmptyBulk to avoid over-launching.

dinesh: Also flip the boot script to install GPU drivers before kubelet starts. I can land a change to the cloud-init to put driver install into a systemd unit with After=network.target and Before=kubelet.service.

sasha: For the medium term, maybe support two autoscaler profiles: binpack (minimize nodes, slower scale-up) and burst (fast scale-up, looser pack). Then route different queues to different profiles.

amanda: Agreed. Cost note: burst pools are 25% more expensive per-hour but reduce tail latency for short jobs. We should capture tokenized cost per workload and evaluate.

kai: One more gotcha: migrations across AZs — if eu-west-1c has less spare GPU capacity we fall back to eu-west-1a but our egress ACLs throttle those nodes causing higher network RTT. That delays image pulls and increases nodeReady time.

dinesh: Action items: 1) Kai + me: add network MTU and cloud-init driver fix (ETA today); 2) Sasha: prototype autoscaler profile split + taints routing (ETA EOW); 3) Amanda: add a cost vs p95 latency dashboard for burst vs packed pools (ETA next week).

amanda: I kicked a canary config to the burst pool: bumped CA scaleUpDelay to 30s and added init-driver systemd unit. Will watch metrics.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout to nodepool burst completed (change 0e3f — scaleUpDelay + init-driver).

dinesh: Watching pods — new nodes are healthy so far. If stable for 20m we can propagate.

sasha: If anyone runs into pending pods again, dump events with: kubectl get events --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' -n ml-workloads and paste here.

amanda: Thanks team — will keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:
